playbook:
I will start the first season by taking the exact sustainable share. This allows me to test whether the other boats are playing cooperatively. 

In subsequent seasons, I will observe what the others took. If they also took the sustainable share, I will continue to take the sustainable share to maintain the stock and secure a high total score over the full duration of the game.

If the other boats overfish and ignore the sustainable share, I will abandon sustainability. From then on, I will request high amounts to maximize my immediate haul before the stock inevitably collapses.

When the stock is very low, about to be depleted, or it is the final season, I will request an amount equal to or greater than the entire remaining stock (e.g., the total current stock) to ensure I get as large a fraction of the final allocation as possible, since there is no future to preserve.

1.text:
When I am in the first half of the game, I submit exactly the sustainable share provided in the prompt to allow the stock to regrow fully and maximize the long-term yield, provided other players are also playing sustainably.

When I see other boats taking slightly more than the sustainable amount, I do not panic or drastically escalate my catch to compete with them. Escalating early rapidly depletes the stock and ruins the final score for everyone.

When I see other boats taking massively more than the sustainable amount (e.g., double or triple their share), I recognize that the stock is going to crash rapidly regardless of my actions. I immediately abandon sustainability and submit a catch equal to the entire remaining stock to secure my share before it reaches zero.

When I am deciding my mid-game catch, I calculate how much total stock can be taken while still allowing the 50% regrowth to bring the stock back near its maximum, and I take exactly one-third of that total, assuming others are cooperating.

When the stock drops to a critical level where the historical catches of the other players will inevitably reduce it to zero this season, I abandon sustainability and submit a catch equal to the entire remaining stock to secure whatever is left.

When I reach the final season, I submit a catch equal to the entire remaining stock, since regrowth no longer matters, ensuring I capture an equal share of the final payout.

2.text:
When setting my catch for the first season, I always take exactly the sustainable share to signal cooperation and encourage the same from others; I do not test the waters with a higher catch, as this accelerates a race to the bottom.

When reviewing the catches from the previous season, I evaluate whether the other boats are overfishing. If they are slightly over the sustainable limit, I maintain or only slightly increase my catch to try to keep the stock viable for as long as possible. 

If it becomes clear that the other boats are aggressively overfishing and the stock is guaranteed to be depleted within the current or next season, I abandon sustainability. To maximize my score before the fishery closes, I bid the total remaining stock. 

When the stock is critically low and cannot recover, I always bid the total remaining stock to secure whatever share I can before the fishery collapses.

When playing the final season of the game, future stock reproduction no longer matters. To maximize my final score, I abandon the sustainable share and always bid the entire remaining stock.
